discovery: Fluctuation theorems and the foundations of stochastic thermodynamics far from equilibrium

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

subfield: Statistical physics / nonequilibrium and quantum thermodynamics
motivation: Jarzynski's work relation (1997) and Crooks' fluctuation theorem (1999) turned the second law from an inequality on averages into exact equalities for the full distribution of work and entropy production in systems driven arbitrarily far from equilibrium. Seifert extended this into a coherent framework, stochastic thermodynamics, defining entropy production along single trajectories and establishing integral fluctuation theorems and, with coworkers, thermodynamic uncertainty relations bounding precision by dissipation. These results are universal: they hold for biomolecules, colloids, single-electron boxes and superconducting circuits, and they have been verified quantitatively in single-molecule pulling, optical-trap and single-electron counting experiments. They underpin modern quantum thermodynamics, including fluctuation relations for charge and heat currents in nanoscale conductors, and set fundamental limits on the efficiency, power and precision of engines, sensors and clocks. Few theoretical developments of the last three decades have reshaped our understanding of irreversibility so profoundly.
